verdict: Intuit grew revenue 17% to $4.7B in its pre-tax-season quarter, as QuickBooks' online ecosystem jumped 21% and Credit Karma surged 23%, lifting net income 47% to $693M.

kpis.label: Credit Karma
kpis.note: +23% YoY — personal loans, cards and auto insurance

segments.name: Global Business Solutions
segments.note: QuickBooks and Mailchimp for small and mid-sized businesses. The online ecosystem brought in $2.5B (+21%), with QuickBooks Online accounting revenue up 24% — higher prices, customer growth and a richer mix.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Credit Karma ($616M, +23%), TurboTax ($581M, +12% — early filers, ahead of the Q3 peak) and ProTax for professional preparers ($290M, +7%).

flow.costPlain: Running Intuit's cloud services and customer support ($981M), product costs ($18M), and amortization of acquired technology ($44M).

opex.name: Selling and marketing
opex.note: Selling TurboTax, QuickBooks and Credit Karma — the spend ramps ahead of tax season, when the year's customers are won.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building QuickBooks, TurboTax, Credit Karma and Mailchimp — increasingly, AI agents that do bookkeeping and tax prep.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day.

opex.name: Amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of customer relationships and other assets from acquisitions like Mailchimp and Credit Karma.

otherDetail: Interest and other income, net of $72M, less $58M of interest expense, added $14M.
footerNote: Cost combines Intuit's three reported cost-of-revenue lines.
pngFooterNote: Cost combines Intuit's three reported cost-of-revenue lines.
follow100Note: This is Intuit's build-up quarter, before tax season peaks: it kept $14.90 of every $100 — compare the Q3 tax-season quarter, when it keeps $35.81. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Growth before the main event
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 17% to $4,651M even though Q2 is only the warm-up to tax season. Global Business Solutions grew 18% and Consumer 15%, and Intuit reiterated its full-year guidance.

takeaways.title: Credit Karma is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Credit Karma revenue jumped 23% to $616M on personal loans, credit cards and auto insurance, while TurboTax grew 12% to $581M on early-season filers.

takeaways.title: Profit grew much faster than sales
takeaways.text: GAAP operating income rose 44% to $855M and net income 47% to $693M, as revenue growth outran a 16% rise in running costs. GAAP EPS was $2.48; non-GAAP EPS was $4.15.
